clue.text: Responsible for worker being late

parts.note: to be behind something is to be responsible for it
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A worker turns up late and someone is to blame for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means running behind schedule, so it is a synonym of late.

clue.text: Confuse married American during social gathering

indicators.note: something happening during an event takes place inside it

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work or fun, as in a sewing bee
M is the abbreviation for married
US for American

explanation.surface: A married American is bewildered at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a communal gathering, as in a spelling bee or quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse is to puzzle or bewilder someone, a synonym of confuse.

clue.text: Her book on capital generated by plant

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
the capital of France

explanation.surface: A woman's book about a capital city spawned by some factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only sets the book next to the capital. 'Plant' looks like a factory but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Paris is a woodland flowering plant with a single berry, Paris quadrifolia.

clue.text: Is one expected to stand for it?

definitions.text: Is one expected to stand for it?

parts.words: Is one expected to stand for it?
parts.note: surface reading: asking whether something must be tolerated or put up with
setter's reading: people rise to their feet when a country's official song is played

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for' suggests tolerate; the setter means literally getting up on your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences customarily rise when a country's official song is played at ceremonies and sports events.

clue.text: Home from a short spell in Panama?

indicators.note: a thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a Panama is a brimmed straw hat
a bit is a short while

explanation.surface: Coming home after a brief stay in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama here is the straw hat, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Fabric having a fine edge after Anns embroidery

indicators.note: after puts the edge word behind the jumbled name
embroidery embellishes and works threads into new patterns, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Ann; the S is the possessive, Ann's
a keen blade has a sharp edge

explanation.surface: A cloth with a delicate hem following some needlework by a woman called Ann.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as Ann's embroidery: the S is only the possessive, so the name alone is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Content of the picture Ben Hur, say

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it, so the letters are found within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Describing what the film Ben Hur contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Hur is a famous example of a grand historical film of the kind called an epic.

clue.text: Simple map I found enclosed

indicators.note: something enclosed is shut inside another thing

parts.note: a plan is a map or drawing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A basic map with a letter I marked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unadorned or straightforward, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Exclusive groups, terribly esoteric

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so the letters are mangled into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cliques that are extremely obscure to outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small closed circle of people sharing an interest, so the plural means exclusive groups.

clue.text: Novel rich wise editor revised

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy, wise editor reworks a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's 1959 book about his Cotswold childhood, often called a novel.

clue.text: What movement of timer could be worth

indicators.note: moving the letters around shifts them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering what value the ticking of a clock might have.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is a synonym of worth: the quality of deserving praise or value.

clue.text: Gourmet may be tense after examination in German city

indicators.note: coming after places the tense letter at the end of the rest
one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the oral exam goes within the city

parts.note: Bonn, the former West German capital
a viva is an oral examination at university
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A food lover gets nervous after sitting an exam in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva (viva voce) is the oral exam a British student may face; Bonn was West Germany's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant is someone who enjoys good food and drink, close in sense to a gourmet.

clue.text: Drink wine second

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: An order to drink a wine as the second course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads like a number but is the verb: to second a motion is to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it formally, so the verb is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: End of the article, in part, backed girl

indicators.note: the earlier letters are placed in the next word, sitting inside it
something backed is moved backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

indicators.note: 'End of' keeps only the last letter of 'the'

parts.note: the final letter of 'the'
an indefinite article

explanation.surface: A phrase about the end of a newspaper article that some girl supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' means placed inside the word for part, and 'backed' turns that word round before the other letters go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a woman's first name, and crosswords often define names with 'girl'.

clue.text: Pop song, 'Dead End Street'?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1985 single by the band Talking Heads
second meaning: a street that leads nowhere, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead End Street' is itself a Kinks song, so the quotation marks tempt you to name that record; read it literally instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a Talking Heads hit and a fair description of a cul-de-sac that leads nowhere.

clue.text: Film good-natured jockey

parts.note: easy-going and relaxed
a jockey rides horses

explanation.surface: A film about an amiable jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Delicious food in bar? I am so mistaken

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits being wrong about tasty food served in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, and the word now means anything delicious to eat.

clue.text: Male with two small sons entering such a state, possibly the Bay State

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
S is the abbreviation for son, twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man and his two little boys arrive in some state, perhaps the one nicknamed the Bay State.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay State is the official nickname of the US state of Massachusetts, from Massachusetts Bay.

clue.text: Emma, for example, needs two drugs

parts.note: the first drug, the opiate
the second drug: E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman called Emma is dependent on a pair of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma is the title character of Jane Austen's novel, so she exemplifies a leading female character.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Woodhouse is the central female character of Austen's novel, an instance of the answer.

clue.text: Sip neat rum — that's wise?

indicators.note: rum is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters come out oddly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether drinking undiluted rum is the sensible choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink to be sipped, but it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a literary word for having great wisdom and discernment.

clue.text: My clue involved a college

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are twisted together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter's clue concerned a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum, after Aristotle's school in Athens, is a place of learning such as a college or lecture hall.

clue.text: Bird, duck, included in list

indicators.note: something included in a thing is held inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A bird, specifically a duck, appears on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a second bird but gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male chicken, chiefly in American usage, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: A hero around Chicago airport

indicators.note: turned around, the letters are moved out of their original order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A heroic figure hangs about the airport in Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Hare International is the main airport serving Chicago, named after a naval aviator.

clue.text: Paint a picture of fish by harbour

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An artist painting a fish beside the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places the harbour word beside the fish word, here in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent, literally or in words.

clue.text: Not the sort of drink you'd want in the jungle?

definitions.text: Not the sort of drink you'd want in the jungle?

parts.words: Not the sort of drink you'd want in the jungle?
parts.note: surface reading: a beverage you would not order while trekking through the jungle
setter's reading: a pub drink of lager and cider whose name is also a jungle injury from a reptile

explanation.walkthrough: The drink is a British pub mix of lager and cider; in the jungle the same word is a venomous wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the beer-and-cider drink also names an injury from a serpent, which no one wants in a jungle.

clue.text: Plant in southern border

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A plant growing in a flower border in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests a garden bed, which suits the surface, but it gives a word for an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Adult novel develops in a different way

parts.note: A is the film rating abbreviation for adult
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A book for grown-ups takes its story in a fresh direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something anew is to do it again in a fresh or changed manner.

clue.text: King muttered mysteriously about large percussion instrument

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
done mysteriously, the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A monarch mumbling cryptically about a big drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum, or timpano, is a large bowl-shaped drum in the orchestra's percussion section.
